# Yair Walton

> Yair Walton builds community programs and the operating systems underneath
> them, and works on the harder problem of measuring whether they reach the
> people they are meant to reach. Based in Cincinnati, Ohio.

## Who he is

Yair Walton builds things that do not exist yet. He works on the human side and
the systems side at once, and spends most of his time getting people, technology,
and institutions to hold up something none of them could hold up alone.

He has worked with communities in Ukraine, Costa Rica, Argentina, Lithuania, and
Israel. He now works in Cincinnati, where he directs a program working against
isolation among older adults that has reached more than 1,200 people since 2020.

He designed an engagement scoring model when attendance stopped answering the
question, and he and his colleagues built evaluation infrastructure in Salesforce
connecting participant data to outcomes. An independent three year evaluation
found reduced isolation and improved access to resources.

He was ordained at Hebrew Union College in 2021. He lives in Cincinnati with his
wife and their young daughter.

## The idea he works on

Belonging is not a feeling that happens to people. It shows up in who gets the
invitation, who can physically get there, who owns the next handoff, and whether
anyone notices when a person stops coming. Those are design decisions, and
decisions can be made differently.

Counting attendance is easy. The harder question is who is showing up, who is
missing, and whether a person who looks connected on paper actually is. A number
can be technically correct and still answer the wrong question.
